source_text: Οἱ δὲ παραδιδόντες τὰ μυθοποιηθέντα ὑπὸ τῶν ποιητῶν οὐδεμίαν ἀπόδειξιν φέρουσι τοῖς ἐκμανθάνουσι νέοις, καὶ ἐπὶ ἀπάτῃ καὶ ἀπαγωγῇ τοῖ ἀνθρωπείου γένους εἰρῆσθαι ἀποδείκνυμεν κατ᾿ ἐνέργειαν τῶν φαύλων δαιμόνων. Ἀκούσαντες γὰρ διὰ τῶν προφητῶν κηρυσσόμενον παραγενησόμενον τὸν Χριστόν, καὶ κολασθησομένους διὰ πυρὸς τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων, προεβάλλοντο πολλοὺς λεχθῆναι γενομένους υἱοὺς τῷ Διῒ, νομίζοντες δυνήσεσθαι ἐνεργῆσαι τερατολογίαν ἡγήσασθαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τὰ περὶ τὸν Χριστὸν καὶ ὅμοια τοῖς ὑπὸ τῶν ποιητῶν λεχθεῖσι. Καὶ ταῦτα δ᾿ ἐλέχθη καὶ ἐν Ἕλλησι καὶ ἐν ἔθνεσι πᾶσιν, ὅπου μᾶλλον ἐπήκουον τῶν προφητῶν πιστευθήσεσθαι τὸν Χριστὸν προκηρυσσόντων. Ὅτι δὲ καὶ ἀκούοντες τὰ διὰ τῶν προφητῶν λεγόμενα οὐκ ἐνόουν ἀκριβῶς, ἀλλ᾿ ὡς πλανώμενοι ἐμιμήσαντο τὼ περὶ τὸν ἡμέτερον Χριστόν, διασαφήσομεν. Μωϋσῆς οὖν ὁ προφῄτης, ὡς προέφημεν, πρεσβύτερος ἦν πόντων συγγραφέων, καὶ δι᾿ αὐτοῦ, ὡς προεμηνύσαμεν, προεφητεύθη οὕτως· Οὐκ ἐκλείψει ἄρχων ἐξ Ἰούδα καὶ ἡγούμενος ἐκ τῶν μηρῶν αὐτοῦ, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ᾧ ἀπόκειται· καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται προσδοκία ἐθνῶν, δεσμεύων πρὸς ἄμπελον τὸν πῶλον αἰτοῦ, πλύνων τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ ἐν αἵματι σταφυλῆς“. Τούτων οὖν τᾶν προφητικῶν λόγων ἀκούσαντες οἱ δαίμονες Διόνυσον μὲν ἔφασαν γεγονέναι υἱὸν τοῦ Διός, εὑρετὴν δὲ γενέσθαι ἀμπέλου παρέδωκαν, καὶ ὄνον ἐν τοῖς μυστηρίοις αἰτοῦ ἀναγράφουσι, καὶ διασπαραχθέντα αὐτὸν ἀνεληλυθέναι εἰς οὐρανὸν ἐδίδαξαν. Καὶ ἐπειδὴ διὰ τῆς Μωϋσέως προφητείας οὐ ῥητῶς ἐσημαίνετο, εἴτε υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ παραγενησόμενός ἐστι, καὶ εἰ ὀχούμενος ἐπὶ πώλου ἐπὶ γῆς μενεῖ ἢ εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνελεύσεται, καὶ τὸ τοῦ πώλου ὄνομα καὶ ὄνου πᾶλον καὶ ἵππου σημαίνειν ἐδύνατο, μὴ ἐπιστάμενοι εἴτε ὄνου πῶλον ἄγων ἔσται σύμβολον τῆς παρουσίας αἰτοῖ εἴτε ἵππου ὁ προκηρυσσόμενος, καὶ υἱὸς θεοῖ ἐστιν, ὡς προέφημεν, ἢ ἀνθρώπου, τὸν Βελλεροφόντην καὶ αὐτὸν ἐφ᾿ ἵππου Πηγασου, ἄνθρωπον ἐξ ἀνθρώπων γενόμενον, εἰς οὐρανὸν ἔφασαν ἀνεληλυθέναι. Ὅτι δὲ ἤκουσαν διὰ τοῦ ἄλλου προφήτου Ἡσαΐου λεχθέν, ὅτι διὰ παρθένου τεχθήσεται καὶ δι᾿ ἑαυτοῦ ἀνελεύσεται εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, τὸν Περσέα λεχθῆναι προεβάλλοντο. Καὶ ὅτε ἔγνωσαν εἰρημένον, ὡς προλέλεκται ἐν ταῖς προγεγραμμέναις προφητείαις, Ἰσχυρὸς ἁ ς γίγας δραμεῖν ὁδόν“, τὸν Ἡρακλέα ἰσχυρὸν καὶ ἐκπερινοστήσαντα τὴν πᾶσαν γῆν ἔφασαν. Ὅτε δὲ πάλιν ἐμαθον προφητευθέντα θεραπεύσειν αὐτὸν πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ νεκροὺς ἀνεγερεῖν, τὶν Ἀσκληπιὸν παρήνεγκαν.
pass_a_gloss: The ones handing down the things mythologized by the poets bring no proof to the young people being instructed, and we demonstrate that they are said by deception and leading astray of the human race according to the activity of the evil demons. For having heard through the prophets the Christ being preached as about to come, and the impious among men being punished by fire, they advanced that many were said to have been born sons of Zeus, thinking they would be able to effect a wonder-telling to lead men astray about the things concerning the Christ and similar to the things said by the poets. And these things were said both among the Greeks and among all the nations, wherever the prophets were more likely to be believed as preaching the Christ. That they, hearing the things being said through the prophets, did not understand accurately, but imitated the things concerning our Christ as being led astray, we will make clear. Moses the prophet, as we previously said, was older than the writers of histories, and through him, as we previously indicated, it was prophesied thus: A ruler will not fail from Judah and a leader from his thighs, until he comes to whom it has been reserved; and he will be the expectation of the nations, binding his donkey to a vine, washing his robe in the blood of a grape. Therefore, having heard these prophetic words, the demons said that Dionysus was a son of Zeus, and they handed down that he was the discoverer of the vine, and they write that a donkey is led in the mysteries of asking, and they taught that he was torn apart and went up into heaven. And since through Moses' prophecy it was not clearly indicated whether the one coming is a son of God, and whether being carried on a donkey he will remain on earth or go up into heaven, and the name of the donkey and the name of the ass could signify both donkey and horse, not knowing whether the one being preached is a symbol of the presence of asking, leading a donkey, or a horse, and whether he is a son of God, as we previously said, or a son of man, they said that Bellerophon, a man born from men, went up into heaven on the horse Pegasus. That they heard through another prophet, Isaiah, that he will be born through a virgin and will go up into heaven through himself, they advanced that Perseus was said. And when they learned that it was said, as previously spoken in the aforementioned prophecies, The strong giant will run the road, they said that Hercules, strong and having run around the whole earth, was so. When, however, they again learned that he was prophesied to heal every disease and raise the dead, they brought forward Asclepius.

bible_refs.note: A ruler will not fail from Judah and a leader from his thighs, until he comes to whom it has been reserved; and he will be the expectation of the nations, binding his donkey to a vine, washing his robe in the blood of a grape

pass_b_english: Those who pass on the myths invented by the poets offer no proof to the young people they instruct, and we demonstrate that these stories were spoken through the deceptive activity of evil demons to lead the human race astray. Having heard through the prophets that the Christ was about to come and that the impious among men would be punished by fire, the demons promoted the idea that many men were born as sons of Zeus, thinking they could pass off the facts about Christ as mere wonder-tales similar to the poets' fictions. This was done both among the Greeks and among all nations, wherever the prophets were most likely to be believed as heralds of the Christ. We will make clear that, although they heard the prophetic words, they did not understand them accurately but imitated the truths concerning our Christ while being led astray. Moses the prophet, as we have said, was older than all historians, and through him, as we previously indicated, it was prophesied thus: "A ruler will not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his loins, until he comes to whom it is reserved; and he will be the expectation of the nations, binding his donkey to a vine, washing his robe in the blood of the grape" (Genesis 49:10-11). Having heard these prophetic words, the demons claimed Dionysus was a son of Zeus, handed down that he discovered the vine, wrote that a donkey is led in the mysteries, and taught that he was torn apart and ascended to heaven. Since Moses' prophecy did not clearly indicate whether the Coming One is the Son of God, whether he would remain on earth riding a donkey or ascend to heaven, and since the term used could signify either a donkey or a horse, the demons did not know whether the predicted figure would lead a donkey as a symbol of his presence or ride a horse, or whether he would be the Son of God or a son of man. Consequently, they said that Bellerophon, a mere man, ascended to heaven on the horse Pegasus. When they heard through the prophet Isaiah that he would be born of a virgin and ascend to heaven by his own power, they advanced Perseus as a counterfeit. And when they learned the words, "The strong one like a giant will run his course," as spoken in the earlier prophecies, they claimed Heracles was that strong figure who traversed the whole earth. When they further learned he was prophesied to heal every disease and raise the dead, they brought forward Asclepius.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex theological argument regarding the demonic imitation of prophecy. Pass A preserves the Greek syntax and nuances (e.g., 'wonder-telling' for τερατολογίαν). Pass B provides a fluent English rendering that maintains the meaning and correctly identifies the scripture allusion (Genesis 49:10-11) which was present in the Greek text as a quotation.
